assumptions.text: A US departure order reflects the State Department's own security assessment.

test.rule: Read the departure sentence and the advisory's stated reasons

assumptions.text: Cordon's phrase set catches every departure order and suspension in the advisory text.

test.rule: Every posture change is flagged for review; tests cover the known wordings

assumptions.note: There is no machine-readable field and the wording varies: Saudi Arabia (23 Oct 2026) said staff were 'ordered ... to leave'. Russia's text says its consulates suspended operations, which Cordon does not count as the embassy's.

assumptions.text: State's country codes map to the right ISO country.

test.rule: Tests compare every FIPS mapping with the advisory's own country name

assumptions.note: 14 advisories use ISO or State's own codes (for example Switzerland 'SR'); the title decides for those.

assumptions.text: US embassy alert feeds are reachable.
assumptions.note: On 31 Oct 2026 every post site served a 'Technical Difficulties' page (HTTP 403). Cordon keeps trying and shows no data until they recover.
